code_paper_alignment.methodology_matches.reason: The paper says relaxation acts after every ASAP-scheduled layer throughout the measurement pipeline. The energy/connection implementation instead executes gates in their original order and flushes relaxation when an encountered layer index increases; subsequent gates assigned to earlier layers execute after relaxation already applied to those layers. This changes both channel placement and duration. Static accounting from the saved U10 trivial endpoint gives 78690 microseconds of rotation-circuit relaxation under this implementation versus 86670 under the stated ASAP schedule.
evidence: proposal/report.tex:260-277 specifies all-qubit relaxation for every ASAP layer and applies the full model to prefix and energy circuits.

proposal/code/noisy_eval.py:113-141 flushes the current layer before later encountering gates with smaller assigned layer indices; lines 226-240 use this function to generate the saved probability caches.
proposal/code/compile.py:109-127 collects gates into complete ASAP layers, and proposal/code/noisesim.py:236-246 executes those layers; this differs from the prefix implementation.
proposal/logs/trajectory_U10_trivial.npz, ops_x/ops_z endpoint selections: read-only gate accounting gives 78690 versus 86670 microseconds, excluding preparation and measurement-basis layers.

The saved first rotation already yields H on qubit 0 assigned to layer 6 but executed when cur_layer=7; proposal/code/compile.py:16-39 and proposal/code/noisy_eval.py:124-138 expose this ordering directly.
